transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess it’s probably not a huge thing, but it’s been getting in the way. I keep sort of planning my day around avoiding those really high bridges when I have to drive. And if I can’t avoid one, I get through it, but I’m gripping the wheel pretty hard the whole time. Does that make sense?
Is your discomfort specific to certain types of bridges, like high or crowded ones, or does it happen on all bridges regardless of how they look or feel?

It’s more the high ones, especially the ones going over the bay. I mean, I know they’re built fine and people drive over them all day long, so I feel a little silly saying it, but when I’m coming up on one my mind kind of goes to, “What if the car went over the side?” Not every little bridge does that to me.
Do you ever feel this way when you’re not actually on or near a bridge, like maybe just thinking about driving over one later in the day?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, if I know I have to go that way I might kind of think, “Ugh, I’d rather not,” but I wouldn’t say I feel the same as when I’m actually coming up on the bridge. Is that the sort of thing you mean?

When you know you'll have to drive over one of those high bridges later, do you feel anxious beforehand—like hours or even a day in advance—or does the anxiety only start when you're actually approaching the bridge?

It’s mostly when I’m actually getting close to it. Like, I can know earlier that day I’ll have to cross it and I’m not thrilled about it, but it’s not too bad. Then as soon as I see the bridge coming up, my chest gets tight, my hands get sweaty on the wheel, and I kind of just stare straight ahead like, okay, just get to the other side. I know that probably sounds a little dramatic, but that’s about how it feels.
Do you ever feel this kind of anxiety in other situations, like being in open spaces, crowds, or when you're away from home, or does it only happen when you're near high bridges?

No, I don’t think it’s crowds or being away from home or anything like that. It’s really just those high bridges, especially over the bay. I know they’re built fine and people drive them every day, but when I get near one, my mind just goes to this thought like the car could go right over the side. I know that probably doesn’t make much sense.
Has this fear of driving over high bridges ever caused you to significantly change your routine or avoid certain places altogether, even if it’s inconvenient?

Yeah… I mean, I probably wouldn’t say it’s taken over my life or anything, but yes, I do plan around it more than I’d like to admit. I’ll look for routes that don’t make me go over those high bridges, even if it adds time. And if there’s no real way around it, I’ll do it, but I’m pretty tense the whole way—just gripping the wheel and trying to get across. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you're approaching one of those high bridges and start feeling anxious, do you notice your heart racing, feel short of breath, or experience any other strong physical sensations along with it?

Yeah, I guess there are some physical things. It’s not like I’m completely falling apart or anything, but when I see the bridge coming up, my chest gets tight and my hands get sweaty on the wheel. I tend to just stare straight ahead and focus on getting to the other side. Is that what you mean?

Does this fear or discomfort happen only when you're the one driving over the bridge, or does it also happen when you're a passenger or even just thinking about crossing a high bridge in another way, like on foot?

It’s mostly when I’m actually near one, especially those high bridges over the bay. I know they’re built fine and people go over them all day long, but my head still jumps to, you know, what if the car went over the side. I realize that probably sounds a little dramatic, but that’s the thought that comes up.
Have you ever felt this kind of anxiety or had these physical feelings in situations where you aren't near a bridge, like in open spaces, enclosed spaces, or when you're far from home?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I can get stressed like anybody, but those same feelings… I haven’t really noticed them unless it’s something to do with those high bridges. Open spaces or being far from home, that doesn’t really ring a bell for me. Is that helpful?
Have you ever had these anxious feelings or physical sensations, like a racing heart or sweating, in situations where you aren’t near a high bridge or planning to cross one?

Not really, no. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but it’s pretty tied to seeing the bridge coming up. As soon as I notice it ahead, my chest tightens up, my hands get sweaty on the wheel, and I kind of lock my eyes forward like I just need to get across. But away from that situation, I can’t say I really get those same feelings.
Do you ever feel this kind of anxiety or get those physical feelings in other situations—like if you're up high in a building, near water, or even just driving on regular roads?

No, not really in those other situations. I mean, heights in a building or regular driving don’t usually bother me like that. It’s more those bridges over the bay. I know they’re built fine and people drive them every day, but when I get near one, my mind kind of jumps to the car going over the side. I know that probably sounds silly, but that’s the part that gets to me.

Do you ever feel this kind of anxiety or get these physical feelings—like a tight chest or sweaty hands—in response to other specific things, like flying, getting an injection, seeing a spider, or something else like that?

I don’t think so, no. Flying isn’t something I do much, but I don’t remember feeling that same tight-chest, sweaty-hands thing with stuff like shots or spiders. It really seems to be just the bridge situation, as far as I can tell. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you ever had a strong physical reaction, like a tight chest or sweaty hands, when you’ve come into contact with other specific things, like spiders, storms, needles, or anything else like that?

Not really with those things, no. I mean, if we’re talking about the strong physical reaction, it’s when I see the bridge coming up. That’s when my chest gets tight, my hands start sweating on the wheel, and I just kind of stare straight ahead like, “just get to the other side.” I don’t notice that with spiders or needles or storms, at least not like that.
